jia (DevEx): Quick sync — seeing intermittent token refresh failures in the Kotlin client after we rolled shading changes. Root error looks like NoSuchMethodError/ClassCast between jackson and gson during streaming responses. Anyone seen this pattern?

tom (client-eng): Ugh. Can you paste the stacktrace and the gradle shadow/relocate rules? Also which okhttp version?

jia (DevEx): Stack (trimmed):
```
java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: com.fasterxml.jackson.core.JsonFactory.createParser(Ljava/io/InputStream;)Lcom/fasterxml/jackson/core/JsonParser;
 at com.ourlib.streaming.NDJsonReader.parse(NDJsonReader.kt:48)
 at com.ourlib.client.StreamingResponseHandler.handle(StreamingResponseHandler.kt:22)
Caused by: java.lang.ClassCastException: com.google.gson.internal.bind.ReflectiveTypeAdapterFactory$Adapter cannot be cast to com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonDeserializer
```

leah (build): Checklist: shadow plugin versions? Are we relocating both com.fasterxml.jackson and com.google.gson, or only one? If both are present at runtime, classloader will pick wrong impl.

ben (eng-runtime): Two things to check: interceptor order in OkHttp and shading relocations. For OkHttp, if you add Authorization header in a network interceptor it can get dropped on redirects. Use application interceptors or mutate the request before proceed. Example (Kotlin):
```
val authInterceptor = Interceptor { chain ->
  val req = chain.request().newBuilder()
    .addHeader("Authorization", "Bearer $token")
    .build()
  chain.proceed(req)
}
client = client.newBuilder().addInterceptor(authInterceptor).build()
```
Also ensure you call newBuilder().followRedirects(true) appropriate to your flow.

jia (DevEx): Interesting — the failing cases were during reconnect after 307 redirect. We were using a networkInterceptor. Switching to addInterceptor fixed header loss in a local repro.

tom (client-eng): Nice find. For the serialization clash: sounds like both gson and jackson types are visible and our shading didn't fully relocate jackson-databind's internal packages. In shadow plugin we should relocate com.fasterxml.jackson -> com.redwood.shaded.fasterxml.jackson and same for gson. Also ensure generated service loader files (META-INF/services) are merged or remapped; Jackson uses module registration via ServiceLoader sometimes.

leah (build): Agreed. Gradle shadow snippet we used previously:
```
shadowJar {
  relocate 'com.fasterxml.jackson', 'com.redwood.shaded.fasterxml.jackson'
  relocate 'com.google.gson', 'com.redwood.shaded.gson'
  mergeServiceFiles()
}
```
Make sure mergeServiceFiles() is present otherwise you get mixed impl registrations.

ben (eng-runtime): For streaming with Jackson, prefer streaming API (JsonFactory/JsonParser) not mixing with Gson. In our case some transitive lib was using Gson to parse a chunk and Jackson to parse the wrapper — that caused adapter/class cast issues when both classes are present with same names. Shading both and merging service files resolved it for me previously.

jia (DevEx): Thanks. I'll open a small PR with two changes: 1) move auth header to application interceptor + add test for redirect, 2) update shadow relocates and mergeServiceFiles. @leah can you review the shadowJar part when I push? Link: <https://github.com/redwood-inference/client/pull/1234>
